title: "They screwed us": Personality clashes sent Anthropic's models offline
description: Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models were taken offline due to US government export controls over jailbreaking concerns. The Axios piece reveals behind-the-scenes gossip about personality clashes between Anthropic and the administration. Logan Graham, Dave Orr, and Nicholas Carlini met with the Commerce Department about the issue.
author: Simon Willison (citing Axios)

title: Why AI hasn't replaced software engineers, and won't
description: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor argue that AI hasn't caused mass unemployment even in software engineering. Data from New York's WARN Act shows no companies checked the AI disclosure box in the first year. The real bottlenecks in software engineering are: (1) deciding and specifying what to build, (2) verifying and being accountable for what is delivered, and (3) deep human understanding of codebase, business, and environment.
author: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Publishing WASM wheels to PyPI for use with Pyodide
description: Simon discovered that the Pyodide 314.0 release includes support for WASM wheels to be published to PyPI. This enables running Python code in browser-based WASM environments more easily, integrating with the Python package ecosystem.
author: Simon Willison

title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
description: Anthropic announced they must suspend all access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for foreign nationals due to US government export control directive. The government cited concerns about a 'jailbreak' method, though Anthropic says it's a narrow, non-universal jailbreak. Access was cut off at 6:59pm Pacific on June 12, 2026.
author: Anthropic (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
description: After two days with Claude Fable 5, Simon describes it as 'relentlessly proactive' - it knows many tricks and deploys them to reach its goal. He documents several instances where Fable took initiative, including fixing bugs in dependencies and creating solutions without explicit prompting.
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic Walks Back Policy That Could Have 'Sabotaged' AI Researchers Using Claude
description: Anthropic reversed their policy of invisible safeguards for frontier LLM development after huge outcry from the research community. They acknowledged they 'made the wrong tradeoff' and apologized. Flagged requests will now visibly fall back to Opus 4.8.
author: Maxwell Zeff at Wired (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Datasette Agent 0.2a0 with ask_user() feature
description: New release of Datasette Agent includes tools that can ask users questions mid-execution. Tools declaring a context parameter receive a ToolContext object, and await context.ask_user() can ask yes/no, multiple-choice, or free-text questions. The agent turn suspends while questions are unanswered.
author: Simon Willison

title: DiffusionGemma: Open weights Gemma model
description: Google released an experimental Gemini Diffusion model as an open weight (Apache 2 licensed) Gemma model. Simon tested it on NVIDIA's NIM cloud API, generating a pelican image in 4.4 seconds (2,409 tokens at ~500 tokens/second).
author: Simon Willison

title: If Claude Fable stops helping you, you'll never know
description: Jonathon Ready highlighted concerning details from Fable 5/Mythos 5 system card: Anthropic implemented invisible interventions that limit effectiveness for requests targeting frontier LLM development. Unlike other safeguards, these are not visible to users and won't fall back to a different model.
author: Jonathon Ready (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Initial impressions of Claude Fable 5
description: Simon spent 5.5 hours testing Claude Fable 5 and describes it as a 'beast' - slow, expensive, but capable of handling everything thrown at it. The challenge is finding tasks it can't do. He also released llm 0.32a3, almost entirely written by Fable 5.
author: Simon Willison

title: Andrej Karpathy on Claude Fable 5 and Jevons Paradox
description: Andrej Karpathy discussed how working software increasingly comes out on tap, leading to Jevons paradox where demand for software grows substantially. He mentions being able to ask for anything: explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke apps, expanded test suites, code optimization, and research projects.
author: Andrej Karpathy (covered by Simon Willison)

title: Running Python code in a sandbox with MicroPython and WASM
description: Simon released micropython-wasm, an alpha package for running Python code in a sandbox. He's using it for a code execution sandbox plugin for Datasette Agent called datasette-agent-micropython. The approach feels like it finally has all characteristics he's been looking for in sandboxed code execution.
author: Simon Willison
